parts.name: heart_risk_model
parts.original_hypothesis: The predicted risk is a sigmoid of the sum of the six parts: the direct linear score plus five single-unit terms (vessels, absence of exercise angina by sex, fixed thallium defect by fasting blood sugar, ST depression above a threshold, atypical angina). The parts add on the log-odds scale: the output node weights the six part outputs (weights in the formula evidence), and no unit takes another unit's output as input, so the parts interact through the sigmoid and not before it. The direct terms carry most of the model: switching them off moves training AUC from 0.9437 to 0.8381, while switching off a single unit moves it to 0.9388 (fixed defect), 0.9400 (ST depression), 0.9408 (vessels), 0.9418 (exercise angina) or 0.9434 (atypical angina). The inputs restecg, exang:1, slope:3 and thal:3 are unconnected entry nodes: switching them off changes the prediction of 0 training rows. Self-probe (exercise angina, ST depression of 2 mm, a reversible defect and a flat slope held fixed; sex and vessels crossed): the predicted risk is 60% for a woman with 0 vessels, 98% for a man with 0 vessels and above 99% for a woman with 2 vessels, so sex and vessels each move a high-risk profile far, as predicted from their direct weights. The annotated model reproduces the original network on the training rows (largest difference 2.2e-16).

parts.name: direct_terms
parts.original_hypothesis: The direct input-to-output edges form a linear score, the backbone of the model. Through their own edges (logit per sd of the z-scored column), more vessels coloured by fluoroscopy (ca, 2.06), male sex (sex:1, 1.66), a flat ST slope (slope:2, 1.30), higher cholesterol (1.07), asymptomatic chest pain (cp:4, 0.62), higher resting blood pressure (0.62) and a reversible thallium defect (thal:7, 0.46) raise the score; typical angina (cp:1, -0.92), non-anginal pain (cp:3, -0.97), high fasting blood sugar (fbs:1, -0.67), an upsloping ST segment (slope:1, -0.50) and a higher maximum heart rate (thalach, -0.42) lower it; age (0.21) adds a little. The edges for female sex (-0.070) and atypical angina (-0.057) are small. High fasting blood sugar lowering the score runs against domain sense. Ca and sex also act through units (vessels_gate, no_exercise_angina_gate), so their whole-model effects differ from these direct weights. Switching every direct edge off (each replaced by its training mean) moves training AUC from 0.9437 to 0.8381 and flips 45 training predictions, the largest loss of any part. Self-probe (typical case, cholesterol swept): the direct score rises by a steady step per added amount of cholesterol, from -2.65 logit at 150 mg/dL to -0.42 at 250 mg/dL and 1.81 at 350 mg/dL, and the predicted risk from 3% to 74%, as predicted. The closed form (in the formula evidence) is off by up to 0.024 from coefficient rounding.

Through this unit, the mean contribution is -3.19 logit for the 10 fixed-defect patients with normal fasting blood sugar and -0.017 logit for the 5 with high fasting blood sugar. This regime is fitted to 10 rows and runs against domain sense: for the typical training case the model gives a fixed defect with normal sugar a predicted risk of 1%, below the 20% it gives a normal scan, although 60% of the fixed-defect training patients have the outcome. In the whole model these patients still average a predicted risk of 56%, because their direct terms average 2.84 logit. Self-probe (typical case, thallium result crossed with fasting blood sugar): the unit contributes -3.19 logit for a fixed defect with normal sugar, -0.017 with high sugar, and 0.00 for a normal scan or 0.00 for a reversible defect, as predicted. parts.name: vessels_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: The number of major vessels coloured by fluoroscopy (ca) raises the predicted risk through this unit as well as through its own direct edge, and the unit adds more with each extra vessel. The unit is on for every training patient (242 of 242, share 100%), so on these data it never acts as a gate: it is a second linear term in ca, plus a small term for the thal:4 column, a thallium code held by 2 training patients (too few to read anything into). Direct and through-the-unit effects differ: ca's own edge is 2.06 logit per sd, while for the typical training case this unit's contribution goes from -0.42 logit at 0 vessels to 0.18 at 1 vessels, 0.78 at 2 vessels and 1.38 at 3 vessels (contributions are relative to the unit's training mean). In the whole model the typical case's predicted risk climbs from 20% at 0 vessels to 82% at 1 vessels and 99% at 2 vessels, mostly through the direct edge (over the first step the direct terms go from -0.64 to 1.67 logit, this unit from -0.42 to 0.18). Self-probe: in the ca sweep above the unit's contribution rises from -0.42 to 1.38 logit, as predicted. Switching the unit off (holding it at its training mean) moves training AUC from 0.9437 to 0.9408. The closed form relu(weighted ca + weighted thal:4 + bias) is off by up to 0.0014 from rounding of its coefficients.

parts.name: atypical_angina_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: This unit gives patients with atypical angina a small extra decrease in predicted risk. On the training data it is on for the 42 patients with atypical angina (42 have it): there are 0 patients with another chest-pain type on whom it is on and 0 with atypical angina on whom it is off. Its size is small: for the typical training case it contributes -0.044 logit, and switching it off moves training AUC from 0.9437 to 0.9434. The ordering of chest-pain types comes from the direct terms, not from this unit: for the typical case the predicted risk is below 1% with typical angina, 1% with non-anginal pain, 5% with atypical angina and 20% when asymptomatic. Self-probe: in the chest-pain sweep the unit is 0.288 for atypical angina and 0.00, 0.00 and 0.00 for the other three types, as predicted. This part is described rather than explained: it is a constant offset on one chest-pain type that duplicates the direct cp:2 edge (-0.057 logit per sd), with no domain reading beyond that. The closed form is off by up to 0.0018 from coefficient rounding.

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients

confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
